You will be Valiantys’ global owner of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and Developer Experience (DevEx) practice.

description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role

Commissioning is where an AI factory becomes real. As Senior Director, Global Commissioning & Handover, you will lead commissioning of DSX facilities and network across all of Volta's sites, taking each one to ready for service and handing it over to our operations teams.

You will build and lead a global team that owns Volta's commissioning standards for electrical, mechanical and CDU scopes, systems security, commissioning planning, facilities readiness and operational readiness. Your team sets how commissioning is done on every site, from tagging through to the turn-up sequence, and holds the schedule that takes each facility live.

Time to market matters here. You will align commissioning to the turn-up sequence so that commissioning accelerates service rather than delays it, and you will make sure that when a building is handed over, the operations team, the procedures and the systems are ready to run it.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Lead commissioning of DSX facilities and network infrastructure across Volta's AI factories, taking each site to ready for service.

  • Build and lead the global Commissioning and Handover team, covering electrical, mechanical and CDU commissioning standards, systems security, commissioning planning, facilities readiness and operational readiness.

  • Own Volta's commissioning standards for each discipline, from tagging and method statements through each commissioning level to the turn-up sequence.

  • Own CDU installation and commissioning standards, including handover to operations.

  • Own the commissioning schedule for every site and its alignment to turn-up, so that commissioning is never the critical path to service.

  • Deliver the physical and systems security requirements for each site from construction through tohandover.

  • Set the facilities readiness and operational readiness standards and governance, so each facility is ready for operations and the operations team is ready to run it.

  • Lead handover into service, working with DC Operations on acceptance, documentation and training.

  • Work with Design and Engineering, the regional delivery teams and the DSX execution and network teams so commissioning is integrated into the master schedule on every site.

  • Report commissioning progress and risk across sites, and feed lessons learned back into the standards and the reference design.

What You Bring

  • Experience leading commissioning of hyperscale data centres, including electrical, mechanical and liquid cooling systems. Data centre experience is essential.

  • A track record owning commissioning and handover across multiple concurrent sites at this level, and the ability to run it from day one.

  • Deep knowledge of commissioning levels, integrated systems testing and the turn-up sequence for high density GPU environments.

  • Experience with CDU and liquid cooling commissioning and handover into operations.

  • Experience setting readiness governance and handing live facilities over to operations teams.

  • Experience building and leading commissioning teams and managing commissioning agents and contractors.

  • Understanding of physical and systems security requirements in mission critical facilities.

  • Willingness to travel to sites across Europe and North America.

263

 

What We Offer

At Volta, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and able to grow. We're building a company where you can make an impact, keep a healthy balance between work and life, and build a career you're proud of.
As a global team, we do our best to provide great benefits wherever you're based. While some benefits vary by country due to local regulations, we believe looking after our people is simply the right thing to do.

  • Competitive salary based on the work you do here, not your previous salary

  • Equity in Volta, giving you the opportunity to share in the company's long-term success

  • Retirement/pension contributions

  • Comprehensive health, wellbeing and insurance benefits

  • Generous number of vacation days each year

Additional Information

Background Checks

Screening is carried out by Zinc, an accredited third-party provider, after an offer is made and all information is handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable data protection law.

Equal Opportunity

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Accessibility

Candidate Privacy Notice

Your data will be shared only with those involved in the hiring process and will not be used for unrelated purposes. For details, see our Recruitment & Candidate Privacy Notice.

Note to Recruitment Agencies

Volta does not accept unsolicited CVs or candidate profiles from recruitment agencies. Any unsolicited submissions, including those sent directly to hiring managers or employees, will be treated as the property of Volta. No agency fees will be payable unless a valid, signed recruitment agreement is in place, and the agency has been specifically engaged for the relevant vacancy.

title: Principal Technical Program Manager - Technical Strategy Development
location: Mountain View, California, United States | San Diego, California, United States
description:
The Tech Strategic Programs organization delivers for Intuit and Tech Strategy by transforming and driving how our 10,000-person Technology ecosystem operates to accelerate outcomes for our customers.  This high performing team works with senior leaders and partners across the company.  We focus on strategic planning, the operating rhythm, executive narratives, workforce programs, and developing portfolio insights to accelerate the delivery of the highest priority areas for growth and customer impact leveraging emerging technology.

 

We are looking for creative problem solvers with a bias for action, an ability to analyze and connect the dots between multitudinous  sources of data and information, and a strong desire to drive tangible business impact. As a Principal Technical Program Manager, you will work alongside executive leaders to construct and deliver board and C-level content. You will also have an opportunity to work across the broader Product, Marketing, Finance, and Business segment communities to help innovate and drive change in how we operate. This position requires strong strategic problem solving and communication skills, the ability to inﬂuence and develop productive partnerships at all levels of the organization, solid business and technical acumen and a strong understanding of Intuit’s mission and values.


Responsibilities


  • Orchestrate development of executive-level presentations and content to be used by the CTO  in board meetings, CEO Staff meetings, and other forums

  • Partner with senior leaders and cross-functional teams (e.g. Product, Marketing, Finance, Business segments) to outline data-driven strategic frameworks decisions, and actionable recommendations

  • Lead strategy projects / work streams and new initiatives end-to-end, with limited guidance, from initial hypotheses to recommendation to operationalization

  • Develop narratives that highlight the outcomes delivered across the Tech Ecosystem and their connection to strategy

  • Build and maintain strong relationships across the Tech Ecosystem and CTO staff to ensure that we are thinking holistically across multiple tech priorities and in line with our technology strategy.

  • Design and implement frameworks and operating models that accelerate decision making, sharing of best practices, and operational excellence at scale across tech.  


Qualifications


  • 7-10 years of relevant experience in delivering signiﬁcant strategic and operational impact across an organization

  • Strategy and operations experience at a high growth startup, management consulting experience or strategic/analytical roles at large companies is desired

  • Proven track record in leveraging data, developing insight-backed hypotheses and driving learning plans to build compelling business cases

  • Demonstrated business and technical acumen, preferably in a SaaS or platform technology company.

  • Ownership mindset with an ability to convert strategic plans into actions, drive projects to completion, and sweat the details to deliver the outcome

  • Experienced change management leader who is able to inﬂuence and build trust across a highly cross-functional organization (peers, executives and working teams) to accelerate outcomes

  • Excellent communicator with strong presentation skills and compelling storytelling abilities; feel very comfortable leading and facilitating workshops and monthly/quarterly business reviews with executives and teams

  • Highly self-motivated, thrives in ambiguity and able to manage multiple projects with little day to day direction

  • Well-rounded interpersonal skills with the capacity to build relationships with senior stakeholders and collaborate across with team members across varying levels

  • Ability to generate innovative insights, ideas, and opportunities that drive tangible business outcomes

  • FinTech and/or SaaS experience a plus, but not required


Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position will be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

The expected base pay range for this position is:
Mountain View $238,000 - $322,000
San Diego, CA $219,500- $297,000

Who We Are:

We build the intelligence that lets robots sense, reason, and act in the real world, moving beyond the lab and into everyday industrial settings like warehouses and factories. Our technology closes the automation gaps that traditional systems can't solve. We are on a mission to redefine how physical work gets done, and we're looking for curious, bold thinkers to help shape the future of robotics with us.

Overview:

Our AI-driven pick-and-place and returns-handling cells combine robot arms, adaptive force-controlled grippers, AI vision and a safety cabinet, all driven by Cortex, our vision-language-action model. They already run in live customer operations across the EU and US. We are scaling from around 50 units a year to several hundred, and getting there means moving production to external contract manufacturers with full quality control at the supplier. We're looking for a Director of Supply Chain & Hardware Operations to own the path from a release-ready design to a QA'd unit shipped to the customer. You will report to the CEO and receive frozen designs from our Director of Hardware Product Engineering & Industrialization through a shared Design-Transfer Gate.

Your Responsibilities:

Contract Manufacturing & Industrialization

  • Move gripper, cell, cabinet and final assembly to external contract manufacturers and EMS partners, with suppliers building to spec and shipping direct to customers where possible

  • Take frozen designs from Product Engineering into repeatable volume production, including ramp plans, build and work instructions and jigs

  • Run a first pilot build of grippers outside our own facility within your first 90 days

Supplier Management & Quality

  • Select, negotiate with and manage suppliers, including commercial terms and capacity planning

  • Build redundancy for critical single points of failure such as the robot arm and long-lead or sole-source parts

  • Own incoming inspection, supplier quality, first article inspection, PPM targets and the manufacturing side of the RMA process

Planning, Inventory & Logistics

  • Build S&OP, forecasting and buffer stock so parts are staged weeks ahead of each deployment

  • Reduce supplier lead times and keep demo and fleet hardware available

  • Own shipping and import and export across the EU and US

Cost & Operating Model

  • Own hardware unit cost and bring COGS down over time

  • Implement the split between bespoke builds and a standardized product line on the operations side

  • Set up the supply chain operating model, KPIs and review cadence for your function

Qualifications:

Education and Experience

  • 10+ years in supply chain, manufacturing or hardware operations, including several years in a leadership role

  • A track record of taking a complex electromechanical product from prototype to hundreds of units per year, with production that kept running after the ramp

  • Experience standing up outsourced contract manufacturing, supplier quality, logistics and inventory from scratch in a scaleup or growth-stage company

  • Degree in engineering, supply chain, operations or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Skills

  • Hands-on supplier management, including selection, negotiation and supplier quality

  • Manufacturing quality, NPI and industrialization experience

  • Supply and demand planning and inventory management

  • Comfortable installing operating discipline, accountability and KPIs in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment

  • Fluent English and willingness to travel to suppliers and customer sites

Additional Skills / Nice to Have

  • Experience in robotics, warehouse automation, AMRs or autonomous vehicles

  • Experience turning demos and pilots into repeatable production deployments

  • Experience working with product engineering on design-to-cost and DfM

  • German fluency

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary and equity in a fast-growing Series B robotics company

  • Flexible PTO and a collaborative, high-ownership culture

  • Ownership of our supply chain and manufacturing setup as we scale to hundreds of units a year

  • Own the live view of energy availability risk and need: contracted, available, and committed energy and capacity at each site against planned load and ramp, by month and by hour where it matters; keep it current as deals sign, sites come online, and plans change, and close gaps and use surpluses with workload and site planning and energy origination.
